description: The bar chart is designed to illustrate five distinct distribution patterns labeled as 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck.' The horizontal axis categorizes these five distribution patterns, while the vertical axis represents the relative values of each distribution. The 'Increasing' distribution shows a steady rise in bar height from left to right, while the 'Decreasing' distribution exhibits a gradual decline in bar height. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of equal height across all categories. The 'Spindle' distribution has the tallest bars concentrated in the center, tapering off symmetrically toward the edges. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution displays the shortest bars at the center, with the outermost bars being approximately 50% taller than the central ones. Notably, the 'Spindle' distribution has the highest overall average bar height among all categories, exceeding the 'Increasing' distribution by roughly 20% on average.
